A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their complete main texts, Table 1, three algorithm listings, equations, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison; rendered pages resolve text-extraction artifacts.

before.justification: V3 reports theoretical regret guarantees and proofs. Its stochastic hard instances are mathematical constructions, with no experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes reported.

after.justification: V4 remains entirely theoretical, including its revised guarantees and appendix arguments. No original empirical outcomes are reported.

M1.justification: Theorem 4.2 newly specifies using ordinary OSMD while ignoring additional graph feedback when Sα > K, adding a parameter-dependent choice of procedure for general decision subsets. The OSMD-G, swap-rounding, and elimination algorithm listings remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or conducts empirical task evaluations. The added graph construction in Section 4.1 extends a theoretical argument rather than evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baseline comparisons. The newly specified OSMD fallback adds no experimental comparator.

E3.justification: No experimental splits, metrics, training budgets, or testing protocols are introduced or revised. Changes to theorem assumptions concern theory rather than evaluation settings.

E4.justification: Neither version reports empirical ablations, sensitivity studies, robustness tests, or error analyses. The additional construction in Section 4.1 is part of the theoretical reasoning.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, uncertainty estimates, or statistical tests. Appendix D revises a theoretical probability-dependent guarantee, not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: No measured results or experimental findings are added or revised. Table 1 retains the same three asymptotic regret rates; the changed symbolic guarantees concern T1.

T1.justification: Theorems 3.2 and 4.1 add S ≤ K/2. Section 4.1 adds a construction for Sα > K, and Theorem 4.2 adds a guarantee proportional to min{S√(αT), √(KST)}, up to logarithmic factors. Appendix D replaces the additive K + εT terms by Sα, introduces Δ0 = 1, and revises initialization accounting from T0 to SM. These refine existing arguments while retaining the main minimax theorems. Theorem 4.1 still assumes Sα ≤ K, so its new minimum expression does not itself formalize the additional regime.

C1.justification: The abstract and Section 1.2 retain the same central contributions: the graph-feedback formulation, the full-decision-set minimax rate, and OSMD-G using negatively correlated sampling. The secondary guarantee revisions do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 now distinguishes the two Sα versus K regimes and explains when ignoring graph feedback gives a better guarantee. Section 4.2 adds that shared information across parallel systems can make α small. The existing open problems remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The algorithm listings and existing learning-rate, truncation, mirror-map, and elimination-threshold specifications are retained. No implementation, hardware, runtime, code-access, or data-access information is added.

R1.justification: Theorem 4.2 newly incorporates ordinary OSMD's existing semi-bandit guarantee as a complementary bound when Sα > K, modestly refining the relationship to prior OSMD work. The related-work survey, cited works, and overall novelty positioning are otherwise unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized prose expansions in Sections 4.1–4.2 and small wording edits in Appendix E, without section or appendix reorganization. V4 also updates the dates and introduces an '(author?)' citation artifact in Section 4.1.

P2.justification: Added paragraphs and the extra guarantee locally reflow Section 4.1. Appendix E redisplays its inequality without the common η²/2 factor. Table 1 and all three algorithm displays retain their structure and placement; no figures or tables are added.

improvement.justification: V4 adds a useful OSMD fallback that caps the general-subset guarantee by √(KST), up to logarithmic factors, and improves initialization accounting in Appendix D. These strengthen the usefulness and support of secondary results while preserving the central contribution. The improvement is limited by Theorem 4.1 retaining Sα ≤ K despite the new discussion of Sα > K, and by the introduced '(author?)' citation artifact.
